description.describe_ch: 本課程旨在讓學生了解亞太地區的經濟及貿易是如何進行的，並通過學術和實踐討論讓學生對日前經濟趨勢與展望，用專題討論的方式讓學生有更深入的了解。
description.describe_eh: The pupose of this course is to enable students to understand how the economy and trade are carried out in the Asia-Pacific region, and to give students a deeper understanding of the current economic trends and prospects through academic and practical discussions.

targets.describe_ch: 學生具備國際經貿專業知識。
targets.describe_en: Students will demonstrate an understanding of basic knowledge of international economy and trade.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en:
Global Trade Environment: Exchange Rates and International Trade
Reading:
The Economist (Leaders)
“Exchange rates – The symptom, not the cause.”
Learning Guide:
Students should read the assigned article before class and identify key concepts related to exchange rates and international trade. Students are encouraged to underline unfamiliar vocabulary and summarize the article using the 5W1H framework (Who, What, When, Where, Why, and How). During class, students will discuss how currency fluctuations affect export competitiveness and global trade balances.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en:
Pre-class Preparation
• Read the assigned article and identify key economic terms related to exchange rates and international trade.
• Prepare a short summary using the 5W1H framework.

In-class Activities
• Group discussion on the impact of currency depreciation on export competitiveness.
• Case discussion: The weak yen and global trade dynamics.
• Students present their viewpoints on whether governments should intervene in foreign exchange markets.

Post-class Assignment
• Write a short reflection (300–400 words) discussing how exchange-rate movements influence international trade patterns.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en:
Agricultural Trade and Food Security
Reading:
The Economist
“Agriculture in India.”
Learning Guide:
Students should examine the role of agriculture in global trade and the implications of export restrictions and food security policies.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en:
Pre-class
• Read the article and identify key concepts related to food trade and agricultural subsidies.

In-class
• Discussion: Should countries restrict food exports during crises?
• Analyse global food supply chains.

Post-class
• Write a short summary of India’s role in global agricultural trade.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en:
Asia Digital Labour Trade
Reading:
The Economist
“Gig labour in India.”
Learning Guide:
Students should explore the emergence of digital platforms and cross-border service trade in the digital economy.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en:
Pre-class
• Identify key terms such as gig economy, platform labour, and digital trade.

In-class
• Discussion: Can digital work be considered international trade?
• Case analysis of global online labour platforms.

Post-class
• Write a short reflection on digital labour markets.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en:
Trade in Health Services
Reading:
The Economist
“Inbound medical tourism.”
Learning Guide:
Students should analyse the growth of medical tourism and its role in international service trade.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en:
Pre-class
• Read the article and identify key factors driving medical tourism.

In-class
• Discussion: Why do patients travel abroad for medical services?
• Analyse healthcare trade in Asia.

Post-class
• Write a reflection on healthcare services as part of global trade.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en:
Free Trade Port Economy
Reading:
The Economist
“A huge free-trade port.”
Learning Guide:
Students should understand the role of free trade ports and special economic zones in facilitating international trade.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en:
Pre-class
• Identify key concepts such as trade facilitation and free trade zones.

In-class
• Discussion: How do free trade ports stimulate regional trade?

Post-class
• Short report on global free trade zones.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en:
Emerging Global Supply Chains
Reading:
The Economist
“Nigeria and South Africa – Awake, sleeping giants.”
Learning Guide:
Students should analyse the role of emerging economies in global supply chains.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en:
Pre-class
• Identify key terms such as supply chains and emerging markets.

In-class
• Discussion: How do developing economies participate in global production networks?

Post-class
• Reflection on global supply chain transformation.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en:
Indo-Pacific Trade Alliance
Reading:
The Economist
“Australia and Israel.”
Learning Guide:
Students should explore technological cooperation and trade partnerships in the Indo-Pacific region.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en:
Pre-class
• Identify key terms related to trade alliances.

In-class
• Discussion: How do international partnerships influence global trade?

Post-class
• Write a short analysis of regional trade cooperation.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en:
Political Risk and International Trade
Reading:
The Economist
“Japan’s new parties.”
Learning Guide:
Students should evaluate how political changes influence trade policy and economic stability.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en:
Pre-class
• Identify key political-economic concepts.

In-class
• Discussion: How does political uncertainty affect international trade?

Post-class
• Short reflection on trade policy risks.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en:
ASEAN Investment Climate
Reading:
The Economist
“Thailand’s election.”
Learning Guide:
Students should analyse the relationship between political stability and foreign direct investment.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en:
Pre-class
• Identify factors affecting FDI in Southeast Asia.

In-class
• Discussion: How do elections affect investment environments?

Post-class
• Write a short report on ASEAN manufacturing hubs.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Self-learning and Interdisciplinary Learning Week：Students independently participate in international exchange activities, competitions, practical workshops, lectures, internships, study visits, and other events organized by the university, college, or department.

gradeRules.evalb_memo_en: Students are expected to attend classes regularly and participate actively in discussions. Attendance will be recorded in each session. Absences without valid reasons may affect the attendance grade. Active engagement in class activities and discussions is encouraged.

Students are required to complete weekly reading assignments based on selected articles. Assignments may include short summaries, reflections, or discussion questions related to international trade topics. These tasks aim to enhance students’ ability to analyse global economic issues and develop critical thinking skills.

Students will complete a final assignment analysing a current issue related to international trade or global economic development. The project may take the form of a written report or a presentation. Students are expected to apply concepts learned in class to analyse real-world international trade cases.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
Students are expected to attend classes on time and actively participate in discussions. Please complete the assigned readings before class in order to contribute meaningfully to in-class activities. Respectful communication and a positive learning environment are expected at all times.
Students should submit assignments on time. Late submissions may result in a deduction of points unless prior approval has been granted. Mobile phones should be kept on silent mode during class to avoid disruptions.
Any announcements regarding the course will be posted on the iLearn platform. Students are responsible for checking course updates regularly.
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en: Students are expected to adhere to the principles of academic integrity in all coursework. Any form of plagiarism, cheating, fabrication, or other academic misconduct will not be tolerated. All submitted work must be the student’s own original work. If external sources are used, proper citation and referencing are required. Violations of academic integrity will be handled according to the university’s academic regulations.
